summary: Feed s115_double is degraded: IDS is silently dropping 14.8% of frames as oversize (up to 8058B vs 1518B port limit) and receiving 9.6% duplicates, creating visibility gaps and wasted processing.

findings.root_cause: Aggregation of same traffic from multiple TAP/SPAN ingress ports without packet-broker deduplication. 214 of 2230 packets (9.6%) exceed 5% threshold, indicating the same packet is forwarded twice to the IDS feed.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS wastes CPU/memory re-processing duplicates, inflates flow/event counts, skews analytics and can cause false correlations; sustained duplicates increase risk of overload and missed true positives.

recommended_fix.why: Enable broker-based deduplication on the aggregate feed to drop duplicate packets before delivery to the 1Gbps IDS port, restoring accurate traffic volume without losing unique packets.

findings.root_cause: MTU mismatch: upstream network is sending jumbo frames up to 8058 bytes while the IDS ingress port max is 1518 bytes. 331 of 2230 frames (14.8%) exceed the limit, well above 1% threshold.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS NIC drops all oversized frames silently - 14.8% traffic loss. Because this IDS needs_full_payload=true, payload is lost entirely, creating a large blind spot where large-payload attacks, data exfiltration, and jumbo-encapsulated threats evade detection and stateful inspection breaks.

params.suggested_action: enable 9000B jumbo support on IDS NIC/port or normalize upstream MTU to 1500B

recommended_fix.why: Tool requires full payload so broker slicing/trimming to 1518B is not an option (would break IDS detection). Must fix at network/tool layer: either enable jumbo frames end-to-end to the IDS or reduce upstream MTU/encapsulation size to fit 1518B.
